messages:
josh: heads up — customers on dedicated pool `ridge-4b` seeing throughput drop ~60% since 02:10 UTC. p50 latency jumped from 120ms -> ~420ms, lots of 429s. raising an incident, assigning eng-runtime.
maria: on it. any recent deploys to scheduler or batching config?
josh: no deploys from runtime team. autoscaler did one scale-down at 01:58 (small), then a scale-up flurry around 02:12. support ticket mentions sudden client-side timeouts + 'quota exceeded' errors for one tenant at 02:09.
kevin: support here — tenant T-492 hit a billing cap spike but that should only affect their requests, not whole pool. logs show global queue depth grew and batch completion rate dropped.
alex: can you paste the queue debug dump? especially continuous-batcher and scheduler metrics.
josh: pasting snippets: ```
QUEUE_METRICS: pool=ridge-4b depth=432 inflight=32 completed_batches=18/s
CONT_BATCHER: avg_wait=48ms target_wait=15ms fill_rate=0.12
SCHEDULER: max_batch_tokens=128 max_batch_size=8 scheduling_latency_p90=210ms
```
emma: whoa — max_batch_tokens=128 is wrong for most Llama-like models here. We recently rolled a config override from an experiment (compact-mode) and it might have applied cluster-wide by mistake. small tokens -> tiny batches -> throughput collapse.
maria: that explains it. also cont-batcher avg_wait=48ms >> target_wait so it's waiting for tokens to fill but not getting enough because max tokens cap is small. combined with fair-queueing the big-requests from a noisy tenant block batch formation.
kevin: support: tenant T-492 had many short concurrent requests which dominated scheduler slots. they also hit a billing cap, which returned 401 for some requests — causing the clients to retry and amplify load.
alex: next steps: (1) revert the compact-mode override for ridge-4b, (2) bump max_batch_tokens to 2048 and max_batch_size to 64, (3) enable per-tenant admission control to isolate noisy tenants, (4) capture a repro trace.
josh: can someone run the rollback now? I'm still collecting traces.
emma: rolling back config on ridge-4b now. command: ```
curl -X POST "$CTRL_API/pools/ridge-4b/config/rollback" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"key":"compact-mode-override"}'
```
infra-bot: rollback queued on 6 nodes, applying sequentially (ETA ~3m).
maria: while that runs, reproduce locally: set max_batch_tokens=128 in a dev pool and replay the short-request load from T-492. use the replay script: `scripts/replay_concurrent.sh --tenant T-492 --rps 600 --duration 600`
josh: repro performed in staging and confirmed: when max_batch_tokens=128 throughput 55% of baseline, p95 latency jumps. full logs attached: ```
STAGING: run-id=stg-2026-08-12-03
requests_sent=360k successes=358k avg_latency=390ms p95=820ms
batch_sizes: 1:48% 2-4:32% 5-8:15% >8:5%
```
kevin: communicating to customer: "we identified a scheduling config regression that limited batch sizes; we've rolled back the override and are mitigating noisy tenant retries. we'll follow up with RCA and a preserved timeline."
emma: rollback completed on all nodes. monitoring shows queue depth falling and completed_batches rising. new metrics: ```
QUEUE_METRICS: pool=ridge-4b depth=48 inflight=120 completed_batches=78/s
SCHEDULER: max_batch_tokens=2048 max_batch_size=64 scheduling_latency_p90=14ms
CONT_BATCHER: avg_wait=12ms target_wait=15ms fill_rate=0.78
```
alex: nice. action items: - add deploy guard to prevent cluster-wide rollout of compact-mode override - add per-pool config audit and alert when max_batch_tokens < 512 for model families X/Y - implement tenant admission throttle to prevent retries from hogging slots - postmortem + customer comms (kevin/josh).
maria: I'll follow up with a small test that simulates mixed short/long requests to validate fair-queue behavior.
josh: thanks all. tagging incident channel and creating follow-up ticket. :thumbsup:
